newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen kill Algerian union leader in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Algerian union leader in ambush.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists shot dead Algeria's top trade union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda in central Algiers on Tuesday, the Algerian government said.

The shooting was followed less than four hours later by a booby-trapped parcel which exploded in the Algerian garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital, killing one person and wounding 17, the Algerian security forces said.
Four gunmen lay in wait for Benhamouda, a former strong supporter of President Liamine Zeroual and power behind the Algerian leader's election, as he left union headquarters.
"They opened fire on him as he was leaving the UGTA (union) headquarters in Algiers," a resident said.

"They waited for him to reach the last step (of a staircase leading up to the building) and before he could get into his armoured car they emptied at least one magazine into his body. The blood is still staining the ground," a witness said.
The official news agency APS, without giving a source, said Benhamouda's bodyguard had been killed and the warden wounded. It said the ambush took place at 1.25 p.m. (1225 GMT).
In a statement on APS, security forces said Benhamouda, leader of the million-member Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA), was killed in the central May 1st Square.
Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour, in a statement underlining Benhamouda's status, said the death of "an exemplary patriot" was a heavy loss.
He was killed in a "cowardly terrorist attack", said Ben Mansour, using Algeria's official term for killings by Moslem rebels who have been in conflict with the authorities for nearly five years.
About 60,000 people have died, including at least 176 since January 10 when the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan started. The Armed Islamic Group (GIA) had promised to increase attacks during Ramadan.

"The authors of this odious crime...will be hunted and punished with rigour," said Ben Mansour, adding that Benhamouda's death was also "a source of inspiration and example for all in the battle for Algeria to live".

The killing in the heart of Algiers and the parcel explosion in central Blida came just four days after President Zeroual, elected amid heavy security in November 1995, vowed in a nationwide broadcast: "I confirm to the Algerian people the determination of the Algerian state to battle against the terrorist groups until their final eradication."
Benhamouda, a ex-teacher in his 40s, escaped assassination in 1993 when Moslem gunmen machine-gunned his car in Algiers. His brother was shot dead a year later by Moslem rebels.

The UGTA boss was a leading force in Zeroual's election and, back in 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by Islamists, he was instrumental in setting up an anti-Islamist group to support the authorities.
Recently, however, he had shown disillusionment with the country's politicians and said he would form his own party.
New general elections are promised before July this year.
In Paris, union leaders mourned Benhamouda's death, praised his accomplishments and expressed concern at growing bloodshed in the northern African state.
The CFDT, France's biggest union, said it was "in shock following the announcement of the cowardly assassination".

In his last statement this week, Benhamouda had warned citizens of increased violence, saying "don't believe they are targeting only senior political leaders or police, or soldiers. Now they are slaughtering poor and innocent people at random."
